source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #340 (branch fix/312-unaligned-canon-load at head 72c02cd7d00953f47df43bf706a4b8e0c75479f4 — the #312 change (canonical ABI loads and stores trap on unaligned pointers, and the canon-lower trampoline preserves the trap cause instead of flattening it to unreachable) merged with current main bf8de4597b16df23cfb6f5a8b10e71d47faae429 (PRs #326, #336, #337, #338, #339, #341, #343 and #346), with the conflict in canonical.rs resolved by keeping #312's validate_pointer_alignment alongside #322's centralised validate_realloc_result and two test assertions updated to the preserved trap cause; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45565413189, 45565424892 and 45565437460 against the branch and pull-request run 45565338789, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Second re-baseline for PR #340 (#312, canonical ABI loads and stores trap on unaligned pointers, and the canon-lower trampoline preserves the trap cause instead of flattening it to unreachable). After the first re-baseline, PRs #341 (#317, per-instance resource handle tables), #343 (#322, bounds-checked canonical realloc results) and #346 (#333, defined instances materialised in definition order) landed on main, so the branch merged current main again (merge commits 825f42f and 72c02cd, main at bf8de4597b16df23cfb6f5a8b10e71d47faae429) and its CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate again. The merge conflicted in crates/telomere-component/src/runtime/canonical.rs, where #312 added validate_pointer_alignment next to the helper #322 replaced: the resolution keeps #312's validate_pointer_alignment and #322's centralised validate_realloc_result (both function bodies byte-identical to their respective sources), and drops the superseded validate_realloc_pointer_alignment, whose call sites all moved into call_realloc. Two test assertions written against the flattened trampoline behaviour were updated to the preserved trap cause #312 establishes (the latin1+utf16 out-of-bounds shrink test in component_canonical_abi.rs now pins the ‘realloc return: beyond end of memory’ message, and the sibling-handle drop test in component_resource_handles.rs now pins the ‘resource handle 1 is invalid’ message); both tests still require the trap. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45565216579, 45565225662 and 45565239398 on main at bf8de4597b16df23cfb6f5a8b10e71d47faae429; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline). Against this branch's previously checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on 20 of the 32 gated series; on the 12 series of the three configurations that link telomere-component, main measures above that baseline in release (stripped file +1,264 B in component and +1,184 B in wasi and wasi-threads; stripped .text +1,104 B in component and +1,024 B in wasi and wasi-threads) from the #317/#322/#333 code that landed after the baseline snapshot, and below it in release-size (stripped file −2,384/−2,512/−2,528 B and stripped .text −2,256/−2,368/−2,384 B in component/wasi/wasi-threads). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the same 12 series: in release, stripped file +1,520 B and stripped .text +224 B in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads; in release-size, stripped file +1,312 B and stripped .text +1,008 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +10.01% (2,433,656 B to 2,677,280 B), up from +9.90% because the intervening main growth is now reflected in the baseline; the release core-nosimd stripped file series stays at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
